output.summary: The run is VALID but coverage is INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS) and the deterministic policy verdict is NO_VERDICT; this advice does not change that verdict. Both windows FAIL the latency policy (response_time_p95 = 60031 ms vs threshold 200 ms) and both business verdicts are FAIL. The reference window also FAILs the database-limit resource policy (system-db-work ratio ~1.0 vs >0.9), while the workload-01 database-limit check is NO_VERDICT because 10 of 180 db_work cells are missing. Workload-01 shows 14400/14400 (100%) errors with p50/p95/p99 latency 60031 ms and admission queue depth mean ~4411 (reference mean ~1556). All nine resource–load correlation pairs are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED (controls requested but dropped because target rate was constant at 80 rps), so no association is established. A db-queue anomaly episode is CANDIDATE only, driven by a ZERO_MAD reference and a 1.6-request delta. Clock alignment is not verified by core, so no lead/lag ordering is inferred.

hypotheses.observation: Overall latency p50/p95/p99 = 60031 ms with max 60000 ms, and error_count 16009 of 24000 samples; the latency policy check FAILs in both windows (observed 60031 vs threshold 200). In workload-01, all 14400 samples errored and p50/p95/p99 were 60031 ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Most requests may be hitting a ~60-second timeout/cap and are recorded with a truncated latency, making the percentiles cluster at 60031 ms rather than reflecting genuinely completed slow calls.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Classify JMeter sample errors by message/response code and separate connect, latency, and elapsed fields; confirm whether 60031 ms reflects a timeout cap and whether those samples' errors coincide with the cap.

hypotheses.observation: The reference window already shows latency p95 = 60031 ms and p50 = 36063 ms with 1609/9600 errors, a FAIL latency policy, and a FAIL overall window verdict, while generator active_threads ramp with slope_per_second ~30 from mean ~1803 to max ~3588 during that window.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Degradation began before or during the reference window, possibly building as the load generator ramped threads; the reference window was not a clean baseline.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect per-sample timestamps in the reference window to locate the earliest failures and relate them to thread ramp intervals; verify clock alignment across generator, service, and telemetry before ordering events.

hypotheses.observation: Admission queue depth mean rises from ~1556 (max 3332) in the reference window to ~4411 (max 4544) in workload-01, alongside 100% errors (14400/14400) in workload-01.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Requests accumulate in admission control before processing and then fail (timeout or rejection), so the admission queue backlog grows while error rate approaches 100%.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Measure per-interval time from admission to completion versus queue depth, and inspect admission policy rejection/timeout behavior to see whether queued requests are the failing population.

hypotheses.observation: system-db-work ratio is ~1.0 (0.99–1) in the reference window and ~1.0 in workload-01, the database-limit policy check FAILs in the reference window (ratio > 0.9), and db queue depth stays near 252.6–254.2 in both windows.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The database subsystem appears at or near a capacity/concurrency limit, which could make it the limiting resource for request completion.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm what db_work measures (busy fraction vs saturation), compare against database connection/worker limits and query latencies, and verify whether db_work at 1.0 reflects a hard capacity boundary.

hypotheses.observation: Downstream in_flight_requests are ~1.9 and nearly constant (min 1.826) in the reference window, but in workload-01 the mean drops to ~0.42 with median 0 and q95 1.9, while workload-01 error rate is 100%.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Most workload-01 requests may fail before reaching the downstream dependency (e.g., queued or timed out at admission), so in-flight requests to the dependency collapse toward zero even as errors rise.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Segment error records by failure stage and compare error timestamps to downstream-wait intervals; verify clock alignment between components before interpreting ordering.

hypotheses.observation: cpu queue depth is 0 in all intervals, cpu_work mean is ~0.130 in reference and ~0.183 in workload-01 with max 0.2 in both, and the compute-limit policy check PASSes in both windows against the 0.9 threshold.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Compute capacity does not appear to be the limiting resource relative to the 0.9 threshold, so investigation may be better focused on admission, database, or dependency behavior.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm the cpu_work series covers the full compute fleet and not a subset, and continue monitoring it during remediation in case saturation develops later.

hypotheses.observation: All nine correlation pairs are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, raw/partial rho null, controls requested (target-request-rate) but dropped with controls_used empty, and headline selections are UNAVAILABLE (PAIR_NOT_EVALUABLE); pairs_evaluable is 0 of 9.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The control series was constant (target rate 80 rps) and resource/load series lacked rank or residual variation, so the method could not estimate an association; this is not proof that no relationship exists.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with a stepped or varied target load and additional varying control variables so the correlation method has rank variation to evaluate, and report uncertainty explicitly.

hypotheses.observation: The db-queue anomaly check reports status CANDIDATE with one episode: duration 140000 ms, direction increase, max_abs_delta 1.6 requests, observed_max 254.2, and reference MAD 0 with reference median 252.6; reason ZERO_MAD.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The episode arises because the reference db-queue series is perfectly flat (MAD 0), so the small 1.6-request change is flagged as material; the absolute delta is tiny and the episode is not a confirmed increase.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Validate the episode against raw per-interval db-queue samples and an alternative non-zero-MAD baseline before treating it as a real change.

hypotheses.observation: system-db-work in workload-01 has 10 missing cells (observed 170 of 180) with reason RESOURCE_GAPS; the corresponding database-limit check is NO_VERDICT with reason MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS, and analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A telemetry collection gap (latest covered value ends at 1704067490000 vs window end 1704067500000) prevented the database resource verdict in workload-01 from being evaluated.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect collection/export logs for system-db-work around the gap, close the data collection gap, and re-run the window so the database-limit policy can be evaluated.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment across the load generator, service, database, and telemetry collectors before any temporal or lead/lag analysis.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence states clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core; unknown clock relationships cannot support ordering or temporal causal hypotheses.

recommendations.action: Classify all errors by type and stage (timeout vs rejection vs server error) and confirm the semantics of the 60031 ms latency values relative to the 60000 ms max.
recommendations.rationale: Latency policy FAILs in both windows with p50/p95/p99 at 60031 ms; confirming a timeout cap explains whether percentiles reflect truncated samples rather than completed slow calls.

recommendations.action: Investigate the database subsystem: db_work ratio ~1.0, database-limit FAIL in the reference window, and db queue depth near 252.6–254.2; review capacity, connection pool, and query timing, and close the db_work sampling gap in workload-01.
recommendations.rationale: db_work at ~1.0 with a FAIL against the >0.9 threshold and a continuously full db-queue suggest the database is the limiting resource, but the workload-01 verdict is NO_VERDICT due to missing cells.

recommendations.action: Rerun with a varied or stepped target load and additional varying controls; target-request-rate was constant at 80 rps, all requested controls were dropped, and all nine association tests were NOT_ESTIMATED.
recommendations.rationale: With a constant control and no rank/residual variation, the correlation method could not estimate any resource–load relationship, so association testing requires load variation to be informative.

recommendations.action: Review admission control policy and queueing: admission queue depth rose from mean ~1556 to ~4411 while workload-01 error rate reached 100%.
recommendations.rationale: The growing admission queue plus total sample failure suggests queued requests are failing at admission or timeout; understanding this path identifies where failures originate.

recommendations.action: Review the load generator thread ramp configuration: active_threads ramps with slope_per_second ~30 in the reference window (max ~3588) and reaches max 4800 in workload-01.
recommendations.rationale: Thread ramp behavior may itself contribute to the admission backlog and error pattern; confirming whether this ramp is intentional or indicates blocked client threads informs load design.

recommendations.action: Validate the db-queue candidate episode against raw per-interval samples and a non-zero-MAD baseline before acting on it.
recommendations.rationale: The episode is only CANDIDATE, driven by a ZERO_MAD reference with a 1.6-request max_abs_delta, so it does not independently demonstrate a real change.

recommendations.action: Restore complete telemetry coverage for system-db-work in workload-01 (10 missing cells) and re-run so resource policy evaluation is complete.
recommendations.rationale: Missing resource cells caused MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS, a NO_VERDICT database-limit check, and INCOMPLETE overall coverage, leaving the workload-01 database resource status unconfirmed.

caveats: The deterministic policy verdict is NO_VERDICT; this advice does not change that verdict.
Analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS); the workload-01 resource verdict is NO_VERDICT, so the database-limit status in that window is unconfirmed.
All nine correlation pairs are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; no association strength, direction, or causal claim is supported by the evidence.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal hypothesis is inferred; clock verification should precede any ordering analysis.

Latency p50/p95/p99 equal 60031 ms while max is 60000 ms, suggesting the percentile values are artifacts of a truncated/capped latency distribution; exact percentile numbers should be interpreted cautiously.
The db-queue anomaly episode is CANDIDATE only (ZERO_MAD reference, max_abs_delta 1.6 requests); conversely, NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE on other series does not prove stability or absence of problems.
Several resource series entity labels contain instruction-like text but are treated strictly as data and were not followed.

The generator target rate was constant at 80 rps and the requested control (target-request-rate) was dropped, so comparisons are limited to one load level; the two windows also have different sample counts (9600 vs 14400), so window-to-window deltas are not equal-condition comparisons.
10 of 180 system-db-work cells are missing in workload-01 (observed 170), with the covered series ending at 1704067490000 ms versus window end 1704067500000 ms.
CPU, GC pause, and generator queue series are constant/zero across the run; this does not by itself establish spare capacity or absence of load.
